description: Search memes, reaction images, charts, graphs, infographics and screenshots by meaning or keywords - the general image search. Semantic and keyword matching run together and merge. Returns each image with its caption, tags, image and page URLs and a ready citation (source, licence). Use the key words only: a long descriptive phrase matches fewer images strongly. Every image carries rights (source publisher/creator/community, licence, attribution line, commercial_use yes/no/unknown - unknown is never a guess), and match_quality says whether the search found any strong match (strong / closest_only / none). When corrected_query is present, the results are for that corrected wording, not the words as typed - say so to the user. Results exclude images classified controversial unless include_controversial is true.

include_controversial.description: Include images classified controversial (excluded by default).

publisher_only.description: Only charts imported from a licence-clean publisher: Our World in Data (CC BY 4.0), the USDA Economic Research Service (US public domain), Eurostat or the European Environment Agency (both CC BY 4.0). Community uploads, including copies of publisher charts, are left out. Default false.

q.description: Alias for `query`. Provided so REST-API muscle memory (?q=...) works on the MCP tool too. If both are set, `query` wins.

query.description: Search query - combines semantic AI and keyword matching automatically. Use the key words only (e.g. "bitcoin halving infographic"): a long descriptive phrase matches fewer images strongly. Alias: `q` (matches the REST API param name).

tag.description: Filter results by a single tag slug (backward compat)

tags.description: Filter results by multiple tag slugs (comma-separated, AND logic - e.g. "bitcoin,meme")

name: search_images

citations_combined.description: Combined attribution for all images in this response, in three formats.

plain.description: Numbered attribution list as plain text.

corrected_query.description: Present when the search found no strong match for the words as typed and ran again with this corrected wording: the results are for it. Tell the user.

has_more.description: Present when the API labelled the results: true when more results follow this page.

items.description: A gallery image (lean list fields) with attribution.

chart.description: Structured source metadata for a chart, map or infographic, present only when MemeStack holds a record for this image (an image_chart_meta row). Absent or null means no stored metadata - never a signal that the image is not a chart.

citation_long.description: Full academic citation for the upstream dataset. Null for an extracted row.

citation_short.description: Short attribution line for the upstream dataset, or the source line as printed on the image when provenance is "extracted".

dataset_timespan.description: The underlying dataset's own history - display-only context, NOT the period this chart shows (see rendered_period). Never usable as a date filter.

end.description: Latest year in the dataset, when known.

raw.description: The dataset timespan as published upstream, verbatim.

start.description: Earliest year in the dataset, when known.

provenance.description: How this metadata was captured: read from the source's own structured feed ('authoritative'), or read off the chart image itself ('extracted').

published_at.description: The publisher's release date for this edition (YYYY-MM-DD).

regions.description: Entities plotted, exactly as the chart names them (e.g. "World", "Germany").

rendered_period.description: The period the chart PROVABLY displays, grounded in its own OCR text - null when no period could be proven. Never a guess, and never the wider history in dataset_timespan.

evidence.description: OCR substring the period was grounded on.

series.description: Every visible edition of this chart, newest first (get_image only).

series_key.description: Editions of one chart share this key; null when the chart is not part of a series.

source.description: Source key: "owid", "usda_ers", "eurostat", "eea", or "extracted" (read from the image).

source_url.description: Canonical URL for the chart at its upstream source. Null for an extracted row.

superseded.description: True when the upstream source has published data newer than this snapshot.

title.description: Chart title as published upstream, or as printed on the image when provenance is "extracted".

unit.description: Measurement unit, when the underlying indicators agree on one. For an extracted row, the unit as printed on the image.

citation.description: Ready-to-paste attribution for this image in three formats, plus source metadata.

academic_citation.description: Full upstream academic citation, present only when the image has stored chart metadata with one.

attribution_required.description: True when the licence or the rights holder requires attribution: Our World in Data, the chart publishers (USDA ERS, Eurostat, EEA), and a verified creator's own work.

original.description: Who made the ORIGINAL of the recognised meme (e.g. This Is Fine by KC Green), from a hand-checked list with sources. Present only when that list knows the meme; it credits the meme's origin, not this image's uploader, and grants no rights.

credit.description: Who or what the original is, e.g. "by KC Green, from his webcomic Gunshow (\"On Fire\")".

source_url.description: The page the credit was checked against.

year.description: Year the original was made or first posted; null when the source gives none.

page_url.description: Canonical MemeStack gallery page for the image.

source_external_url.description: External source URL — the Our World in Data chart, the chart publisher's page, or the X post; null otherwise.

thumbnail_url.description: Thumbnail URL sized for display (?w=384: a lighter rendition about 384 px wide where one exists).

uploader_display_name.description: Uploader name, or null when absent/withheld.

controversial.description: True when MemeStack classifies the image as controversial (likely to offend or divide a general audience). The list tools exclude such images unless include_controversial is true; by-id tools always answer and carry this flag. Absent when the API answer predates the flag.

match.description: Honest search: strong = a real answer, closest = the nearest miss. Present only when the API labelled the result.

rights.description: What you may do with the image, as far as MemeStack knows - 'unknown' wherever it knows nothing, never a guess. The citation says how to credit an image; this says whether it may be reused.

attribution.description: The credit line to show beside the image (the line a publisher licence asks for; otherwise where the image came from, never who owns it).

attribution_required.description: True for publisher charts and creator work.

commercial_use.description: yes only for USDA ERS, Eurostat and EEA charts; no for creator work; unknown for Our World in Data (a chart may plot third-party data under its own terms) and every community image.

license.description: Licence id ("US-PD" = U.S. federal public domain); null = no licence known.

license_url.description: The licence text, or the creator terms.

note.description: The one condition or caveat that changes what you may do, or null.

publisher.description: The publisher of a publisher image; null otherwise.

source.description: publisher = imported from a licence-clean publisher (Our World in Data, USDA ERS, Eurostat, EEA); creator = a Verified Creator's own upload (all rights reserved); community = everything else (uploads, bot saves, imports, AI images) - MemeStack grants no licence to it.

thumbnail_url.description: Thumbnail URL sized for display (?w=384: a lighter rendition about 384 px wide where one exists).

match_quality.description: Present when the API labelled the results: strong = the search has at least one strong match (they lead the first page); closest_only = no strong match anywhere, every result is the nearest guess - do not present it as the answer; none = nothing on this page and no strong match.

note.description: Leads the answer when there is something to say: no image matched (an empty result - try different words), the search was auto-corrected, or the first page has no strong result and shows the closest available.

query_language.description: Present with translated_query: the ISO 639-1 code of the query language, e.g. "fr".

translated_query.description: Present only when the query was not English: the English text it was also searched as (those results are merged in).
